# dsh-plugin-local-infer
中文 (Chinese)
> For those who want more performance out of their specific hardware than what Unsloth gives out of
ose who want more performance out of their specific hardware than what Unsloth gives out of the box.
A DeepSeek Harness plugin that manages local inference engines:

- llama.cpp
- NInfer
- Hyper-Qwen (vLLM)
- Infernix
- Strata
- ...with more coming soon.
Pick a model and an engine, tune the parameters, watch a live **VRAM Est.** meter, see **hardware wa
rnings** the moment a value (or a parameter itself) is unsafe for the detected hardware, then the pl
ugin manages **build, deploy, and health-check** for each engine and **automatically register it as
a DSH model** once it is confirmed working. No hand-editing of finicky yaml or launchers.

Or add from the DSH Plugin Marketplace.
## Using the plugin
The **Engine settings** card mounts on the Plugins page (older hosts: the Settings page).
- **Pick an engine and model**, then tune the parameters. Each field renders by its type: checkboxes
, dropdowns, sliders, text, directory pickers, and a chat-template combo (known templates plus free

text).
- **Watch the VRAM Est. meter.** It prices weights, KV cache, overhead, and workspace against
your card as you adjust values, and shows the verdict (`fits` / `tight` / `over`) and the largest c

ontext that fits.
- **Read the warnings.** Red banners and inline field warnings fire when a paramet

er value, or the presence of a parameter, is unsafe for your detected hardware.
- **Satisfy the syst
em dependencies.** The panel lists each missing host dependency (docker, CUDA toolkit, ffmpeg, hf CL
I, ...) with its purpose, a copy/paste install string for your OS, and an optional one-click **Run**

(sudo). The **Get** button stays disabled until every dependency reports satisfied.
- **Get.** With
the dependencies satisfied, `Get` syncs the engine's source: it clones the engine's git repo (or th
e **Engine Fork** you provided) into the **Engine Directory** override, or with no override into the
engine default checkout home `~/.cache/dsh/infer/<engine>` (one checkout per engine, derived at run
time and never persisted, never inside a model directory). An existing checkout with local changes
aborts with an alert in **Logs**; a clean one fetches the listed fork (added as its own remote) and
rebases onto the upstream branch. It then runs the system dependencies and the engine's build steps.
Every line streams into the **Logs** section as it lands. `Launch` stays disabled while a Get runs

and re-enables when the build finishes, errors, or falls silent for 2 minutes.
- **Launch / Stop.**
`Launch` deploys the engine (builds the checkout, or pulls the image in docker mode), downloads the

model, starts it, and polls its health endpoint. `Stop` shuts it down.

## Orchestrator package
Local models often struggle with agentic workflows and can't "one-shot" prompts without assistance.
The included **Orchestrator** package gives your model a default prompt that enables that capability
he included **Orchestrator** package gives your model a default prompt that enables that capability.
- **Enable it** on the DeepSeek Harness **Plugins** page: open this plugin's entry and flip the **Or
chestrator** component toggle (the component ships disabled). After first enabling the component, re

start the host so it loads.
- **Edit the prompt** on the **Orchestrator** card that then appears: ch
ange the **Orchestrator Prompt** field and press **Save**. The default text ships in the plugin's `p

rompt.md`; clear the field and save to restore it.
- **It injects while enabled.** With the componen
t enabled, the saved prompt is part of the agent's system prompt for new requests. A Save reaches th
e next request; no restart is needed after Save.
The saved prompt persists to `~/.dsh/local-infer/orchestrator.json`, beside the engine config.
## Supported Platforms
### Operating systems
| OS                           | State     | Notes
| Linux (Debian/Ubuntu, `apt`) | Supported | Install blocks mirror the working NInfer launcher: the

CUDA keyring sequence plus the compile toolchain.            |
| Linux (Arch, `pacman`)       | Supp
orted | `pacman` blocks plus the `/opt/cuda` export lines.

|
| Linux (Fedora, `dnf`)        | Untested  | Command set present, flagged

untested on a live host.                                                               |
| macOS (`b
rew`)               | Partial   | CPU/docker path (llama.cpp). No NVIDIA Container Toolkit on macOS,

so the CUDA engines' docker path is unavailable. |
| Windows (WSL2)               | Untested  | WSL
2 is detected and the dflash2 pin-memory rule fires; the command set is flagged untested.

|
| Windows                      | Partial   | Code paths are only partially written; f
urther development needed.                                                  |
### Engines
| Engine            | Docker        | Local build        | State
| NInfer            | Yes           | Yes (cmake + CUDA) | The reference engine. Measured VRAM model

s for the Qwen 27B/35B artifacts.   |
| Hyper-Qwen (vLLM) | Yes (compose) | No                 | `.e

nv`-driven docker-compose profiles.                                       |
| vLLM              | No
| No                 | Work-in-progress.

|
